title: The Textile Museum opens major Inka textile exhibition in Washington
summary: Weaving an Empire: Textiles of the Inka World reveals how Andean dress and other textiles in the 15th and 16th centuries reflected both the influence of the Inka—who built one of the world’s largest empires, rapidly expanding beyond the Cuzco Valley to occupy much of South America’s western region—and the local styles of communities under Inka rule. On view through December 23, 2026, this is The Textile Museum's first major exhibition of South American textiles in over 20 years. "The Textile Museum holds more than 9,000 Latin American textiles—one of the largest collections of its kind outside the region—and they account for nearly half of our 21,000 handmade textile works spanning five continents and five millennia," said John Wetenhall, director of The George Washington University Museum and The Textile Museum. title: Bertoia's August 28 Automobilia Sale showcased rare items from the David Bausch lifetime collection
summary: A hand-painted polychrome bronze sculpture by Stanley Wanlass (American, b. 1941-) depicting an early touring car overtaking a man on horseback sold for $34,800, and a handsome 1929 Franklin Series 11 sedan automobile chugged off for $13,200 at Bertoia’s August 28 Automobilia Sale. The auction featured automobilia items from the celebrated David Bausch collection, an exceptional assemblage encompassing more than a century of automotive history, advertising and design. title: From Egyptian votives to Roman military power, classical antiquities take focus at Artemis auction
summary: Gods and funerary figures, painted reliefs, precious-metal vessels, imperial portraiture and the equipment of Roman soldiers are among the classical antiquities taking center stage in the September 16 auction presented by Artemis Fine Arts and Arte Primitivo. Spanning more than three millennia of Egyptian, Greek and Roman history, the selection shows how ancient objects could serve religion, commemoration, luxury, political authority and warfare. summary: Woody Auction’s Art Glass & Furniture Auction scheduled for Saturday, October 17th, will be led by an incredible Tiffany Studios “Peony” leaded glass table lamp, followed by an impressive array of art glass, including French cameo, English cameo, Loetz, plated amberina, and a sizable Wave Crest collection featuring the rare Goldfish dresser box. title: Christie's Hong Kong to auction rare purple-pink diamond and Cartier ruby brooch
summary: Christie's announces two leading highlights of its Hong Kong Magnificent Jewels Autumn Auction – an exquisite 8.41-carat fancy vivid purple-pink diamond and diamond ring, and a 10.10-carat ruby and diamond brooch by Cartier. Offered on 24 November 2026 during Hong Kong Luxury Week, the auction will also feature an exceptional selection of coloured gemstones, jadeite jewels, natural pearls, and distinguished creations by celebrated jewellery maisons. The Exquisite Coloured Diamond and Diamond Ring (hero image left) is centred on an 8.41-carat fancy vivid purple-pink diamond, a Type IIa diamond among the rarest and most chemically pure of all diamonds. title: Mauritshuis and Rijksmuseum jointly acquire 17th-century Avercamp winter landscape
summary: The Mauritshuis and the Rijksmuseum have jointly acquired Hendrick Avercamp’s Colf Players on the Ice, painted c. 1625. The acquisition signals the return to the Netherlands of one of the most important winter landscapes in Dutch painting. The 17th-century masterpiece will be shown first in Kampen, the town of Avercamp’s birth, where it will be on display from 3 October at Avercamp Back in Kampen: the 17th Century through the Eyes of Hendrick & Barent. It will then alternate between the Rijksmuseum and the Mauritshuis. The acquisition is an exceptional addition to the Dutch national art collection. "Ice and winter fun have been inextricably associated with each other for centuries here in the Netherlands. Few things bring everyone in the country together like those two things. title: High Museum of Art announces four new board members
summary: The High Museum of Art announced the appointment of four new board members today to serve three-year terms: Nikki Crump, Monica Howard Douglas, Johanna Ellis Reisinger and Dawanna Williams. “As we celebrate our centennial anniversary in 2026, we are looking ahead to the High’s next 100 years, striving to be a dynamic, intentional and essential contributor to the cultural fabric of our city,” said the High’s Director Rand Suffolk. “Our new board members are uniquely positioned to help us achieve these goals, and we look forward to working with them to build a stronger museum.” Nikki Crump is an advertising and marketing executive with more than 20 years of experience leading integrated marketing campaigns for Fortune 500 companies. An arts advocate, Crump has been a member of the planning committee for the High’s David C. Driskell Prize Gala since 2024, helping to shape one of the museum’s signature annual fundraising events. title: Mennello Museum welcomes Abigail Baeza, new Associate Curator
summary: The Mennello Museum of Art welcomes Abigail Baeza as Associate Curator of Art and Education, who will work with the team to help advance access to American art and its multiple narratives through curatorial research, exhibition-making, and new perspectives on American art history, our collection initiatives, and public engagement. Abigail joined the museum this summer and holds an M.A.R. (Master of Arts in Religion) from Yale Divinity School with a concentration in religion and visual art. Before Yale, she earned a B.A. with Honors in Art History from Stanford University. In 2024, she curated Color Deceives: Le Corbusier & Josef Albers, an exhibition spotlighting special collections items in Stanford’s Bowes Art & Architecture Library. She also supported curatorial projects at the Diözesanmuseum Freising in Germany and at Bridge Projects, a contemporary art gallery in Los Angeles. title: MAK presents Kateryna Lysovenko solo exhibition Borderland in Vienna
summary: In the MAK exhibition Kateryna Lysovenko: Borderland, the Ukrainian-born, Vienna-based artist Kateryna Lysovenko combines the language of classical painting with contemporary issues. In paintings—some of which were created specifically for the MAK—and selected watercolors, Lysovenko juxtaposes vulnerable bodies, hybrid beings, and mythological tales with heroic narratives of war. She investigates the connections between the body and ideology, using the medium of painting to make life in war and exile a tangible experience. With her thematic explorations, she opens up spaces for social and political imagination. Lysovenko views painting as a social act and a political medium. Her work is less about illustrating events than about methods of discovering and questioning the world. Her dynamic imagery is based on observations, shifts, and fragments of everyday life. title: Fondation Beyeler unveils Peter Zumthor expansion ahead of autumn preview
summary: The Fondation Beyeler is expanding its ensemble – both physically and conceptually – further strengthening the unique interplay between art, architecture and nature for which it is internationally renowned. During the preview phase (26 September 2026 to 14 January 2027), which begins at the end of September, the first visitors will be able to experience Peter Zumthorʼs new buildings, the expanded and restored Beyeler Park and the redesigned historic buildings for the first time alongside the existing museum building by Renzo Piano. During this phase, special opening hours apply and the number of tickets is limited. title: Ateneum to open permanent children's activity space in 2028
summary: The Ateneum Art Museum, which is part of the Finnish National Gallery, has received a significant bequest of approximately 300,000 euros from a Finnish private individual. The bequeathed funds will be used to develop operations at the Ateneum, including enabling the introduction of a new experiential space for young children. The donor’s wish is that their name is not published. A permanent activity space for children under school age and their families will be opened at the Ateneum in 2028. Part of the bequeathed funds, as well as additional external funding to be collected, will be used to realise the space for children. The concept of the space and its opening date will be announced later. “We want every child to experience the Ateneum as their own. With this bequest, we can finally meet the wishes of our audience by introducing a space where you can relax with small children – which is something we have lacked. title: Regen Projects presents Elliott Hundley solo exhibition Book of Sand
summary: Regen Projects is presenting Book of Sand, an exhibition of new paintings, sculptures, and tapestries by Elliott Hundley. Marking the artist’s seventh solo exhibition with the gallery, the presentation furthers Hundley’s rich, multifaceted approach to materiality through an expanded lens of metacognition and philosophically grounded play. Whereas previous exhibitions have drawn from the subject matter and esprit of Euripidean tragedies, Rilke’s sonnets, and plays by Artaud and Genet, Book of Sand focuses on Hundley’s own exuberant internal universe. With each work in the show, Hundley follows a path of automatism: compiling paint, paper cut-outs, string, encaustic, and other found materials without a predetermined narrative or aim. title: Mazzoleni presents Melissa McGill solo exhibition Watermark in Milan
summary: Mazzoleni is presenting Watermark, a solo exhibition by Melissa McGill in Milan, bringing together a group of recent and previously unseen works developed around one of the central themes of her practice: water as a living presence, a relational force, and an active participant in the creative process. Through recently produced watercolours, works created with natural pigments, photographs, and reworked maps, the exhibition reveals the more intimate dimension of a practice that for over thirty years has evolved between the studio, field research, and public intervention. The common thread running through this body of work is water, understood as a medium capable of establishing relationships between bodies, places, and memories. title: RAF Museum London secures prestigious Sandford Award for heritage learning
summary: The Royal Air Force Museum London has once again been awarded the prestigious Sandford Award, recognising the quality and impact of its learning and engagement programme. The independently judged quality mark for heritage learning assesses education provision at heritage sites across the UK, Republic of Ireland, Channel Islands and Isle of Man. Having previously achieved the award in 2021, the Museum’s renewed five-year accreditation provides independent recognition of a programme spanning History, STEM, Early Years and SEND, with workshops and resources designed around schools’ learning outcomes and the National Curriculum. title: Tenki Hiramatsu debuts new paintings in solo show at kaufmann repetto Milan
summary: The title of this exhibition – Smell of the Lawn – already suggests something that arrives before an image: a scent, a memory, the invisible trace of a place. In Hiramatsu’s paintings, too, recognition comes slowly. Figures, animals, and fragments of landscapes seem to settle onto the surface after the fact, as though they had been waiting inside the paint. A figure observes the hint of a poppy in Red Flower; a bird almost sinks into the dim ground of Life’s Stumbles; in At That Moment, a witch-like figure hovers at the edge of a swampy landscape. These images remain suspended just before they become fully legible, in the moment when a story seems possible but has not yet begun. Hiramatsu’s paintings develop through a patient, layered process. title: Zimmerli Art Museum presents Hank Willis Thomas survey LOVERULES
summary: Hank Willis Thomas: LOVERULES — From the Collections of Jordan D. Schnitzer and His Family Foundation brings together nearly 90 works by conceptual artist and activist Hank Willis Thomas (born 1976; Plainfield, New Jersey). Surveying the artist’s most iconic artworks across a range of media, the exhibition explores how images shape perception, identity, and values. By questioning what feels familiar, Thomas connects historical moments of resistance to our lives today and invites us to remain open to change. The exhibition includes Thomas’s key conceptual series, which often draw on the visual language of advertising to reveal how meaning is constructed and circulated. title: John Dilg debuts new landscapes in first exhibition with Peter Freeman, Inc.
summary: Peter Freeman, Inc. is presenting John Dilg: Once and Future, featuring 13 paintings completed over the last two years. This marks the artist’s first exhibition with the gallery and his first solo presentation in New York since 2021. Drawing from a lexicon of earth tones and stylized iconography, John Dilg creates pared-down landscapes that feel familiar, uncanny, and mystical all at once. He exercises a unique restraint while devising his scenes, which are born out of a process of extrapolating a single detail within a found image or dream into a spare natural setting. This process renders each composition with a sparseness reminiscent of an absence or loss while teeming with potential, inviting the viewer to actively look, consider, and participate in their own narrative-building process. title: The Douglas Hyde announces Rachael Gunning as the fifth Provost's Fellow in Curating
summary: Established in 2020, the Provost’s Fellowship in Curating offers recent graduates of Trinity College Dublin the opportunity to work within The Douglas Hyde over a period of twelve months. Through hands-on work and mentorship, the Fellow is given insight into the daily workings of the organisation and its programme, while contributing to discourses within the Gallery, Trinity College and further afield. The Fellowship, which is generously supported by the Office of the Provost, fosters new generations of arts professionals by giving practical experience of working within one of Ireland’s leading contemporary art spaces. Provost of Trinity College Dublin, Linda Doyle notes, "I want to warmly congratulate Rachael Gunning on receiving the Provost’s Fellowship in Curating at The Douglas Hyde Gallery. title: Museum of Decorative Arts and Design in Riga marks Rūdolfs Heimrāts centenary
summary: From 16 September to 22 November 2026, the Museum of Decorative Arts and Design in Riga hosts the exhibition Rūdolfs Heimrāts 100. Legacy, dedicated to the centenary of the outstanding textile artist Rūdolfs Heimrāts (1926–1992) who was professor at the Art Academy of Latvia and founder of the Latvian textile art school. “I love sitting at the loom and weaving. Everything leading up to that moment is filled with doubt and struggle. All kinds of possibilities surround me, and I could go on considering them endlessly, but once I am at the loom, I can honestly say that I am happy. I prepare for it almost as a ritual: I arrange all my materials, choose the records I want to listen to, and then, with the selected music playing, I weave thread by thread. title: Baltimore Museum of Art opens major solo exhibition of Baltimore-based artist Jerrell Gibbs
summary: This fall, the Baltimore Museum of Art invites visitors to experience a solo exhibition of new works by celebrated Baltimore-based artist Jerrell Gibbs. Featuring approximately 30 paintings, Jerrell Gibbs: Come home with me draws on the artist’s life and memories to explore the universality of human experience. The exhibition evokes the home of the artist’s Aunt Ella as a vital site of gathering—revealing how moments of childhood joy, connections to family and friends, and a sense of home transcend the barriers between people. In a moment of deep national division, Come home with me is a powerful and poignant invitation to uplift and engage with what unites us. The exhibition will be on view from September 16, 2026, through May 2, 2027. Gibbs’s expressive, gestural paintings embrace the language of figuration and abstraction.

title: Tauba Auerbach debuts pointillist foam paintings at Paula Cooper Gallery
summary: Tauba Auerbach is presenting a family of new works in various media, reflecting on currents and concurrence. These will include a new generation of pointillist paintings depicting liquid foams photographed through a microscope. Hand-painted dots gather into refractive images on sprayed panels that float slightly off the wall. Earlier works in the series looked at foam’s architecture; these focus on its interaction with light. Of the material, Tauba has said: “Foam often exists at an edge, like the edge of the ocean or the edge of a glass. It’s the unruly boundary between two domains (liquid and air), where order in the traditional sense breaks down, and a new type of organization emerges.
